text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The World Bank and the IMF announced a total package of $360 million for immediate assistance to Pakistan, expressing satisfaction over various economic measures taken by the government recently.

- Trading volume on the Karachi Stock Exchange soared to a seven-month high on massive buying in selected shares spurred by news of Pakistan's agreement with the IMF on the economic stablisation package.
- Pakistan decided not to contest for a United Nations Economic and Social Council seat in view of intense competition from Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Korea, Syria and Japan.
- India warned that it would review the "entire gamut" of bilateral relations with Pakistan if it failed to protect Indian diplomatic staff in Islamabad, the Press Trust of India said.
- The government is likely to have around $500 million through short-term borrowing in November, said Hussain Lawai, the newly appointed consultant to the Finance Minister.
- The Karachi Chambers of Commerce and Industry decided to oppose the levy pf 2.0 percent service charge on pre-shipment inspection of imports and wants the government to withdraw it.
- Soap prices may rise 20 to 25 percent owing to the 8.5 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar and other upward adjustments in taxes and duties at the import stage.

- The new Finance Minister Naveed Qamar said that the agreement with the IMF "signals sustainability of economic policies, enhanced external sector viability and the strength of long-term prospects of the country's economy".
- A three-member World Bank mission is arriving on an eight-day visit to Pakistan on November 4.
- Retail prices of Suzuki and Yamaha motorcycles were raised by over 2.7 percent by local manufacturing companies.
- Finance Minister Naveed Qamar said that his strategy will be to make the Finance Ministry more open and more responsive to the private sector's needs.

- Pakistan warned regional countries against interfering in Afghanistan's internal affairs. A foreign ministry spokesman said any regional conference on Afghanistan not preceded by an intra-Afghan dialogue would be unacceptable to Pakistan.

- Jamaat-i-Islami leader Qazi Hussain Ahmed said he would not take part in the opposition Pakistan Muslim League (PML) rally in Rawalpindi on November 12 as his party was not allowed to put its viewpoint at the PML rally in Lahore on October 27.
